task.goal: A build scheduler runs tasks with dependencies. It currently starts dependents as soon as their parent is started, may run a shared dependency twice, and never rejects cycles. Fix schedule(tasks, runner) in scheduler.py. Run each task once only after all dependencies have succeeded; preserve declaration order among ready tasks; stop on the first runner failure; raise ValueError for unknown dependencies or cycles before running any task. Run visible tests and validate.

result.text: I'll inspect the scheduler and its tests first.Fixed `schedule` in scheduler.py: it now resolves the graph up front (raising `ValueError` for unknown dependencies or cycles before any runner call), then runs each task exactly once in declaration order among ready tasks and propagates the first runner exception. Verified with the visible unit tests and edge-case checks (shared dependency once, diamond graph, declaration-order ties, unknown dep, cycle, chain, failure stops the run).
